title: A Passivity Obstruction: Why a Derived a0 = cH_Lambda/Z and Single-Metric Weak Lensing Cannot Coexist in de Sitter-Unruh Modified Inertia
description: The de Sitter-Unruh modified-inertia (MI) program reproduces galaxy dynamics through a passive vacuum-response kernel K(Box_u/a0^2) whose bounded, causal, positive-measure structure ties the MOND acceleration scale to the cosmological horizon, a0 = cH_Lambda/Z with Z = sqrt(32pi/3) = 5.789. CREDIT UP FRONT: the interpolating nu-kernel law is Milgrom's (Phys. Lett. A 253:273, 1999); the framework's distinctive content is the cH_Lambda/Z coefficient (his was 2cH_Lambda) and the covariant MI completion. What the passive kernel fixes is the SCALE of a0; its numerical value and the sign s = -1 remain postulates -- a one-parameter effective-field-theory reframing, not a first-principles value. This paper asks whether the SAME field theory can also reproduce the weak-lensing MOND relation: the phantom mass (nu-1)rho whose gravitational signature makes the observed lensing radial-acceleration relation coincide with the dynamical one, an equality that excludes single-metric pure MI at ~27 sigma (Brouwer et al. 2021, conservative rail). Conditional on the kernel-passivity premise, it cannot. Writing D (a0 enters solely as the horizon-floored argument of the passive kernel), S (single-metric, c_gamma = c_GW), G (ghost-free), and L (the theory reproduces g_lens = nu g_bar -> sqrt(a0 g_bar), null geodesics feeling the phantom), the central result is D and S imply not-L. Equivalently {D,S,L} is the unique minimal unsatisfiable subset of {D,S,G,L}: each proper subset is realized -- {D,S} is pure MI; {S,L} is the Deffayet-Esposito-Farese-Woodard / AeST class with a0 a free coupling; {D,L} is a disformal two-cone construction that keeps a0 derived but is excluded observationally by GW170817 (Abbott et al. 2017, |c_gamma/c_GW - 1| < 1e-15), violating S. Ghost-freedom G enters no step of the argument. The mechanism is a passivity/amplification dichotomy: the static on-shell dressing K = 1/nu is a bounded (Bernstein-type) function with sup K = 1 at the Newtonian end, so a passive kernel can only SUPPRESS the source to rho/nu, whereas MOND-lensing demands ENHANCEMENT to nu*rho, strictly outside the passive cone. A local curvature term is additionally mass-blind (the phantom it sources scales as sqrt(M), under-lensing a cluster by ~41x when fixed on a galaxy); the true phantom is nonlocal in the baryons (point-mass enclosed M_ph(r)/r -> sqrt(a0 M/G)), so any L-realizing term is a distinct nonlocal carrier whose acceleration scale is a free Lagrangian coupling. The obstruction is explicitly CONDITIONAL on the passivity premise -- but that premise is precisely what derives a0, so within the passive class the derivation and not-L are consequences of one hypothesis; whether any non-passive (pumped) kernel could derive a0 is a separate open question that the banked sign walls shut pump-free. Consequences: a complete single-metric, GW-safe field theory reproducing MOND lensing does exist -- but only as modified GRAVITY, with a0 a free coupling (the Deffayet-Woodard / AeST class), which forfeits the program's most distinctive claim; weak lensing is thereby a shared modified-gravity observable and no longer discriminates MI from MG, so the clean MG-impossible discriminator reverts to the non-adiabatic relational velocity-dispersion spread (MI 6-13%, MG exactly 0). The obstruction vindicates the a0 reframing as load-bearing: its distinctive content is exactly what is incompatible with single-metric MOND lensing. All a0-valued numbers are reported on both footings (9.36e-11 canonical rho_DE/cH_Lambda; 1.13e-10 alternate rho_total/cH0); the verdict is footing-independent. This is a conditional obstruction, not a closure of the program. Not a theory of everything -- the a0 reframing and its field theory only. Every load-bearing claim is backed by a committed, adversarially verified, exit-0 script.
notes: Referee-graded writeup (draft -> 4-reviewer adversarial panel -> revise); the panel caught and fixed a kernel function-class error (the static on-shell dressing K = 1/nu is a bounded Bernstein-type function, K(0)=0 rising to sup K = 1 at the Newtonian end, NOT completely-monotone; sympy-verified) and recast the theorem from a spurious XOR to the implication D and S imply not-L. Companion to 'MI Field Theory Results 2026' (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21403470), which flagged the lensing sector as the program's one open failure; this paper resolves it as a conditional obstruction. Both a0 footings carried on every dimensional number. Milgrom 1999 credited as the identical nu-kernel; Deffayet, Esposito-Farese & Woodard 2011 (PRD 84, 124054) and Skordis & Zlosnik 2021 (AeST) credited as the {S,L} modified-gravity class; Bekenstein 2004 (TeVeS) as the two-metric lensing lineage; Brouwer et al. 2021 as the ~27 sigma benchmark; Desmond-Hees-Famaey 2024 for the inherited Cassini Q2 caveat. a0's value and the sign s=-1 remain postulates. No 'proves / solved / complete field theory' language. https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula
